# About

This report shows predictions for a predictive model trained on
**`{python} USERNAME`**'s board game collection in order to identify which new and upcoming
releases they are likely to own and which older games closely
match their taste. The model is trained using features observable at
release (categories, mechanics, designers, publishers, playing time, estimated complexity) in order to predict games *before* the BGG community has weighed in.

For more on the model's findings and evaluation, see the companion
[Model Report](`{python} f"model/{USERNAME_SLUG}.html"`).

```{python}
#| label: predictions-setup
#| include: false
# Shared setup for the prediction sections below: build the `upcoming` frame
# (recent/upcoming releases scored by the model) and the status lookup once.
status_lookup = build_status_lookup(data.collection)
finalize_through = arts.registration.get("finalize_through")
upcoming = arts.upcoming_predictions.join(data.games, on="game_id", how="inner")
if finalize_through is not None:
    upcoming = upcoming.filter(pl.col("year_published") > int(finalize_through))
upcoming = upcoming.sort("predicted_prob", descending=True)
```

# New on BGG {#new-on-bgg}

Games recently added to BoardGameGeek that the model has scored for the first
time in the **last 7 days** — a running look at what the model makes of brand-new
releases as they appear. The **Prediction** is the model's call at its tuned
threshold.

```{python}
#| label: predictions-new-7d
#| column: page-right
if "is_new_7d" in upcoming.columns:
    _new = upcoming.filter(pl.col("is_new_7d")).sort("predicted_prob", descending=True)
else:
    _new = upcoming.head(0)

if _new.height == 0:
    print("_No games newly scored in the last 7 days._")
else:
    from src.reports.tables import format_new_games_table

    _new_table = format_new_games_table(_new, threshold=arts.threshold, top_n=50)
    # Columns: Image0 | Game1 | Description2 | Pr(Yes)3 | Prediction4
    itables_show(
        _new_table,
        paging=True,
        pageLength=10,
        classes="display compact",
        columnDefs=[
            {"className": "dt-center", "targets": [0, 3, 4]},
            {"width": "70px", "targets": [0]},
            {"width": "220px", "targets": [1]},
            {"width": "80px", "targets": [3]},
            {"width": "110px", "targets": [4]},
        ],
        style="width: 100%",
        allow_html=True,
    )
```

# Top Picks {#top-picks}

## New and Upcoming Games

::: {.column-margin}
Games are ranked and sorted based on the model's predicted probability; the top games might have a relatively low probability if the user has a relatively small collection.
:::

Predictions for recent and upcoming releases for **`{python} USERNAME`**. Filtered to games published *after* the model's training window
(`finalize_through`). The **Status** column shows whether the game is
already in the user's collection.

```{python}
#| label: predictions-upcoming
#| column: page-right
# `upcoming` and `status_lookup` are built in the predictions-setup cell above.
from itables import JavascriptFunction

_upcoming_table = format_predictions_with_images(
    upcoming,
    status_lookup=status_lookup,
    top_n=100,
    show_actual=False,
)
# `_is_new` is the last column (index 6): Rank0 Image1 Game2 Desc3
# Pr(Yes)4 Status5 _is_new6. Hide it and use its value to tint the
# row for games first predicted within the last 7 days (mirrors
# bgg-dash-viewer's NEW signal; soft green = same family as its badge).
_IS_NEW_COL = list(_upcoming_table.columns).index("_is_new")

itables_show(
    _upcoming_table,
    paging=True,
    pageLength=10,
    classes="display compact",
    columnDefs=[
        {"visible": False, "searchable": False, "targets": [_IS_NEW_COL]},
        {"className": "dt-center", "targets": [0, 4, 5]},
        {"width": "60px", "targets": [0]},
        {"width": "90px", "targets": [1]},
        {"width": "200px", "targets": [2]},
        {"width": "80px", "targets": [4]},
        {"width": "100px", "targets": [5]},
    ],
    createdRow=JavascriptFunction(
        f"function(row, data, dataIndex) {{"
        f"  if (data[{_IS_NEW_COL}] === true) {{"
        f"    row.style.backgroundColor = '#d1fae5';"
        f"  }}"
        f"}}"
    ),
    style="width: 100%",
    allow_html=True,
)
```

## Older Games to Check Out

Older games that the model predicted for the user during training and evaluation. These were the highest scoring games that the model identified during training that *were not currently* in the user's collection. 

Note: these are technically 'misses' by the model, but in practice they represent games that are consistent with what is in the user's collection and can be thought of as 'games the model thinks they should check out'.

```{python}
#| label: predictions-older
#| column: page-right
older = (
    pl.concat(
        [arts.oof_predictions, arts.val_predictions, arts.test_predictions],
        how="diagonal_relaxed",
    ).join(data.games, on="game_id", how="inner")
    # `label` is a boolean (or 0/1) here — true = user owns it. We want
    # not-owned games for the recommendations list, so cast and negate.
    .filter(~pl.col("label").cast(pl.Boolean))
    # Drop the label column so the table doesn't render an "Owned"
    # column of all-"no" values.
    .drop("label")
)
if "users_rated" in older.columns:
    older = older.filter(pl.col("users_rated") >= 5)
older = older.sort("proba", descending=True)

# Same image-rich format and Status column as New and Upcoming.
# format_predictions_with_images reads `proba` when `predicted_prob`
# is absent, which is the case here.
older_table = format_predictions_with_images(
    older,
    status_lookup=status_lookup,
    top_n=200,
    show_actual=False,
)

itables_show(
    older_table,
    paging=True,
    pageLength=10,
    classes="display compact",
    columnDefs=[
        {"className": "dt-center", "targets": [0, 4, 5]},
        {"width": "60px", "targets": [0]},
        {"width": "90px", "targets": [1]},
        {"width": "200px", "targets": [2]},
        {"width": "80px", "targets": [4]},
        {"width": "100px", "targets": [5]},
    ],
    style="width: 100%",
    allow_html=True,
)
```
